messages.content: Show me the room-level comparison now. I need to know that Marcus Lee, Daniel Lee, and Owen Lee can all occupy the room, and I don’t want a quoted rate that quietly assumes only two people.

I found a problem with the L’Enfant Plaza results: the available rooms showing two beds are doubles, but the live rate is limited to two registered guests. The qualifying alternative near DCA is Crystal City. I can compare that against Penn Quarter, retaining one room, two standard beds, four nights, and three registered guests. Should I make that substitution?
Yes. Penn Quarter against Crystal City is fine. Keep the museum travel time in the comparison.

Three rooms survive those checks. In Penn Quarter, Embassy Suites Washington DC Convention Center has a two-room suite with two queen beds. The occupancy field accepts three guests, and the hotel confirms a maximum occupancy of six. The four-night total is $1,487.36, including $189.12 in taxes and mandatory fees. Breakfast is included for all three registered guests. Cancellation is free until 11:59 p.m. local time on October 7; after that, the charge is one night plus tax. It is about a 12-minute walk to the National Portrait Gallery and roughly 18-25 minutes by Metro or walking to the National Mall museums.
That sounds workable. What is the other Penn Quarter room?

Riggs Washington DC has a room with two queen beds and permits three occupants, but its total is $1,706.44 for the four nights, including taxes and the mandatory destination fee. Breakfast is not included. Cancellation is free until 6:00 p.m. on October 6, followed by a one-night charge. It has the best location of the three: about 3 minutes on foot to the Portrait Gallery and 10-18 minutes to most Mall museums.
So the extra $219.08 mainly buys the location, and we would still pay for breakfast?
Correct. Riggs is $219.08 more than Embassy Suites before accounting for breakfast. Its principal practical advantage is saving about 5-10 minutes per museum trip, depending on the destination.
All right. Give me the strongest Crystal City option, including the actual door-to-museum time rather than just the train ride.

Hilton Garden Inn Reagan National Airport has a room with two queen beds confirmed for three registered guests, with a maximum occupancy of four. The complete four-night price is $1,106.28, including $142.76 in taxes and mandatory fees. Breakfast is not included; the current breakfast add-on would be $18 per person per day. Cancellation is free until 11:59 p.m. on October 8, then one night plus tax. Allow 30-40 minutes door to door to the Smithsonian station museums: a 7-minute walk to Crystal City Metro, about 10 minutes on the Yellow Line, and another 8-15 minutes of walking and waiting.
Any resort fee, parking charge, or occupancy surcharge missing from that total? We won’t have a car.

No resort or destination fee applies, and the three-person occupancy is already reflected in the $1,106.28 total. Parking would cost extra, but no parking charge is included because the search is for no vehicle. Standard Wi-Fi is included.
For family hotel stays, prioritize free breakfast when there’s a reasonable option. It saves us time in the morning. Don’t let that outweigh a major price or location difference, though.

On this comparison, that moves Embassy Suites ahead of Riggs without making Crystal City irrelevant. Embassy Suites includes breakfast and is centrally located; Hilton Garden Inn remains $381.08 cheaper, or approximately $165.08 cheaper if all three of you bought its $18 breakfast each morning for four mornings.
Is the Embassy breakfast definitely included for a 12-year-old, or is that based on two adults only?

It is included for every registered overnight guest, including Owen at age 12. I checked the three-guest rate rather than relying on the generic amenities description. The room record lists Marcus Lee and Daniel Lee as adults and Owen Lee as a child age 12, with no added breakfast or occupancy charge.
Good. Compare airport logistics. We land at DCA at 8:28 Thursday night and fly out at 6:45 Monday evening.

For Embassy Suites, the simplest arrival is a rideshare or taxi, normally 15-25 minutes at that hour and about $22-$35. Metro is possible in roughly 30-40 minutes with a transfer and a walk, but it is less convenient with luggage. For Hilton Garden Inn, the hotel’s complimentary DCA shuttle is scheduled until 11:00 p.m.; after pickup, the ride is usually 5-10 minutes. For Monday departure, allow 25-40 minutes by car from Embassy Suites and leave around 4:15 p.m. Hilton Garden Inn’s shuttle would support a departure around 4:45 p.m., subject to confirming the day’s schedule at check-in.
Use the hotel shuttle only as the Crystal City plan. For Penn Quarter, assume rideshare both ways. Does Embassy have two actual queen beds, with no sofa bed needed for the three of us?

Yes. The selected suite has two fixed queen beds in the bedroom. A separate sofa bed exists in the living area, but it is not required for the confirmed three-person occupancy. The quoted rate is specifically tied to the two-queen suite, not a king suite with a sleeper sofa.

Then make Embassy Suites the primary and Hilton Garden Inn the fallback. Do not book yet. Restate the exact totals, cancellation deadlines, names, flights, and transfer assumptions so the next step can be a clean booking.

Primary: Embassy Suites Washington DC Convention Center, October 10-14, one two-room suite with two fixed queen beds for Marcus Lee, Daniel Lee, and Owen Lee, age 12. The complete four-night total is $1,487.36 including taxes and mandatory fees; breakfast is included for all three guests. Cancellation is free through 11:59 p.m. local time on October 7, then one night plus tax. Plan on rideshare between DCA and the hotel in both directions.

Fallback: Hilton Garden Inn Reagan National Airport in Crystal City, same dates and guests, one room with two queen beds. The complete total is $1,106.28 including taxes and mandatory fees; breakfast is not included. Cancellation is free through 11:59 p.m. local time on October 8, then one night plus tax. Use the complimentary hotel shuttle from and to DCA, with the return schedule reconfirmed at check-in.

Flights remain the Thursday 5:35 p.m. ORD-DCA nonstop, arriving 8:28 p.m., and the Monday 6:45 p.m. DCA-ORD nonstop, arriving 8:03 p.m. The current airfare is $1,226 for all three travelers with one checked bag each way. Nothing for Washington has been booked.
